# Data card — telco customer-intelligence (synthetic)

**This dataset is 100% synthetic.** It is generated by a seeded program
(`generate.py`) from statistical assumptions. It contains **no real customers,
no employer data, and no data derived from any real telecom operator.** Any
resemblance to a real person or account is coincidental.

## Why it exists

To demonstrate customer-intelligence methods (segmentation, churn, next-best-
offer, ARPU, incrementality) on a shared, realistic-but-open dataset — without
exposing any employer's or customer's data. The narrative is grounded in the
kind of work the author has done; the *data* is fabricated on purpose.

## What it is

- **Population:** configurable (default 5,000 customers), a mix of prepaid and
  postpaid plans across four fictional regions.
- **History:** configurable (default 24 months) of usage, billing, digital
  engagement, support and campaign exposure — all before a single observation
  cutoff.
- **Target:** a 90-day churn label living *after* the cutoff.

## How it was made

A deterministic generator with an explicit causal structure (documented in
`README.md`). Churn is caused by observable trajectories plus unobserved
satisfaction and noise; retention campaigns carry a true but confounded uplift.

## Known limitations — read before using

- **Not a real distribution.** Base rates are chosen to be *plausible and
  instructive*, not to match any specific market. Do not cite any figure from
  it as a real-world statistic.
- **Simplifications:** usage/billing/engagement are aggregated to monthly grain;
  one active subscription spell per customer; a single churn cutoff.
- **The causal parameters are known** (they live in `config.py`). That is a
  feature for teaching — you can check whether a model recovers them — but it
  means the dataset is not a blind benchmark.

## License & reuse

Synthetic data, generated by code in this repository, under the repository's
MIT license. Reuse freely; keep this card with it.
